title: Dashboard Resilience and Query Throttling Guidelines
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures guidelines for making observability dashboards resilient (available and useful) even when the telemetry backend or query layer is under heavy load. It focuses on query-throttling strategies, lightweight fallback widgets, metric definitions that support graceful degradation, and a short incident runbook for dashboard-throttle situations.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Our Grafana/Metabase query budgets are repeatedly hitting spikes during releases and postmortems. Expensive ad-hoc queries can degrade dashboards for everyone.
- Customers and SREs depend on a small set of core dashboards (SLO, ingress latency, KV cache health). When instrumentation queries fail or time out, we lose critical context.
- Need consistent defaults so teams don’t accidentally publish super-expensive panels to org-wide folders.

High-level goals:
1) Ensure a guaranteed lightweight dashboard experience (<= 3 cheap panels) that stays readable even under heavy query backpressure.
2) Define per-widget cost/budget limits and enforce them via query throttling and query planners.
3) Provide metric semantics that allow fallbacks: aggregated counts and approximate percentiles when full-resolution queries fail.
4) Give authors explicit knobs: cost estimate, shard-scope, tenant-scope, sample-rate hints.

Definitions (short):
- Cheap metric: single-point-timeseries or pre-aggregated counters (1s/10s rollup).
- Moderate metric: rollup with small group-by (tenant or model), few cardinality dimensions.
- Expensive metric: high-cardinality group-bys, long time-range raw histograms, or ad-hoc trace joins.
- Dashboard resilience mode: a runtime flag (per-folder) where panels are replaced by fallback widgets when backend load is high.

Suggested metric definitions (so panels can degrade gracefully):
- request.count (counter) — labels: route, model_family, region, tenant_id (optional). Use it as primary volume signal.
- request.latency_p50, request.latency_p95 (precomputed rollups) — store P50/P95 on Prometheus-like store every 10s; fallback to approximate histogram sketches if missing.
- kvcache.hits, kvcache.misses (counters) — prefer counters over gauges for cost.
- token.emit_rate (gauge, sampled) — high-cardinality per-model, but provide aggregated model_family token.emit_rate for dashboard.
- trace.error_count (counter) — anchored to spans tagged with failure=true.
- query.cost_estimate (label on dashboard queries) — human readable token-est or cost units per query.

Instrumentation requirements for resilient panels:
- Always prefer pre-aggregated series for org-wide dashboards. Use rollups (10s or 1m) for any panel that will be in the /shared folder.
- Avoid GROUP BY tenant_id unless the panel is scoped to a tenant-owned folder. If tenant-level breakdown is needed, use a sampled or cached dataset (see Sampling hints).
- Tag metrics with a "cardinality_hint" label at ingestion time (low|medium|high) so query planner can auto-throttle.

Dashboard authoring checklist (to include in dashboard metadata):
- Estimated query cost: LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH
- Max time range default: 6h / 24h / 7d (authors must pick one)
- Default granularity: 1m (org dashboards)
- Allowed panel types: timeseries, single-stat, heatmap (with guardrails)
- Fallback content: short text + last-known good snapshot or cached image URL
- Contact owner + runbook link

Query throttling model (proposal):
- Global query budget per tenant + per-organization pool. Budgets are computed using historical query cost and a small buffer for spikes.
- Each panel registers a cost class: cheap=1, medium=5, expensive=20 (arbitrary units).
- During normal operation: allow best-effort queries up to budget.
- When backend 95th latency > threshold or error-rate > 2%: enter degraded mode. In degraded mode:
  - Block or queue expensive panels (show warning).
  - Replace medium panels with precomputed aggregates or downsampled series.
  - Always render cheap panels.
- Implement progressive backoff for repeated high-cost queries from the same dashboard or user.

Sampling hints & trace anchoring:
- For high-cardinality metrics, accept a sample_rate label at ingestion (e.g., sample_rate=0.01) and expose a sampling-aware UI that scales counts.
- Traces: store a lightweight index by trace-anchor tags (e.g., request_id, tenant_id, route). Dashboards should link to trace samples, but trace queries default to 1/s sampling unless explicitly requested.

Fallback widgets & UX patterns (concrete):
- Last-known-good (LKG) single stat: shows the last successful value and timestamp; cheap to render (cached).
- Snapshot image: pre-captured PNG of a dashboard section (updated on cron or on-publish) used when real queries fail.
- Aggregated summary card: shows volume, p95/end-to-end, error-rate from precompute store and links to the on-call runbook.
- "Cost badge" overlay on panels: shows estimated cost and adds a tooltip why it might be blocked.

Alerting and SLI alignment (suggested):
- SLI: "Core dashboard availability" — percent of time the guaranteed lightweight dashboard responds successfully in a 12h window. Target: 99.9% (org-wide).
- SLI: "Critical panel freshness" — percent of time the SLO panel had data <= 60s stale. Target: 99%.
- Alerts:
  - Dashboard backpressure alert (P0): when > 10% of org dashboards are in degraded mode for 15m. Pager to infra-oncall.
  - Query error surge (P1): backend query error rate > 5% and QPS > baseline for 5m. Ops slack channel and ticket.

Runbook (short) — if dashboards go blank or show throttled messages:
1) Confirm scope: check /observability/metrics/backlog and /observability/query-latency. Is the backend overloaded or is it a query storm?
2) Switch to resilience mode (manual toggle) for org-wide folder — replaces expensive panels with LKG widgets.
3) Identify offending panels: use query logs (trace_id) to find top 10 queries by cost in last 30m.
4) If a specific dashboard or user is responsible, temporarily disable or embargo the dashboard and page the dashboard owner.
5) If it's backend instability (ingestion lag, TSDB GC), escalate to infra SRE and follow the normal backend incident runbook.
6) Post-incident: run a dashboard audit (see "authoring checklist") and add query-cost estimates to any new panels.

Enforcement surfaces (where we implement controls):
- Dashboard editor: require cost class and default range for any shared dashboards; provide cost estimator UI.
- Query gateway: enforces budget and per-user progressive backoff.
- Rendering tier: ability to substitute panel content (LKG, snapshot) when throttled.
- CI check: PRs touching /shared dashboards must pass a light query-cost check before merging to prod folder.

Operational metrics to track the system itself:
- dashboard.render.latency (p50/p95) and dashboard.render.error_rate
- query.gateway.rejected_queries.count (by cost class, by team)
- budget_utilization.percent (per-tenant, per-org)
- snapshot_freshness_seconds (how stale are fallback images)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to compute cost units precisely? (token-based vs query-time vs estimated CPU) — add benchmark matrix.
- Should snapshots be automatically refreshed on dashboard view for a missed-render? (tradeoff: increased load).
- UI: how intrusive should cost badges be for first-time authors?
- Tenant-sensitive panels: best practice for sensitive PII/redaction when caching snapshots.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Diego: prototype query gateway enforcement with simple cost classes (2 week spike).
- Samir: add dashboard editor hooks to require cost class metadata and default range (1 sprint).
- Asha: prepare a shared-folder rollout plan and communication template for dashboard owners (this doc + changelog) (1 week).
- Lina: draft a dashboard CI check for PRs to /shared dashboards (draft spec).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider an "emergency snapshot mode" where we serve a cached lightweight JSON instead of running queries; helpful for on-call postmortems.
- Might want to experiment with automated panel-level downsampling (reduce resolution from 1s->30s) when budget is low.

References and examples:
- Internal: OBS-4123 (query-budget spike during 2025-09 release)
- Confluence draft: Dashboard Config Standards (links above)
- PR: observability#987 (dashboard editor metadata)

Appendix: sample panel metadata YAML (for dashboard authors) — put in metadata field on publish:
---
cost_class: MEDIUM
default_range: 24h
max_granularity: 1m
allowed_groups: [team-internal]
fallback: lkg-single-stat
owner: eng-model-routing
---

End of doc.
